candidate_sentence_map.S1: Coop Pank delivered strong business growth in 2025, although profitability declined as lower interest rates reduced income.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Net profit fell 11% year on year to €28.7 million, from €32.2 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Net interest income decreased 6% to €73.3 million, reflecting the lower-interest-rate environment, while net interest margin declined from 3.8% to 3.0%.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Net fee and commission income increased 4% to €4.5 million, and net other income rose to €1.5 million from virtually zero.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Total net operating income declined 3% to €79.4 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Operating expenses increased 2% to €41.5 million, resulting in a deterioration in the cost-to-income ratio from 49.6% to 52.3%.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Credit loss allowance improved to €3.3 million from €4.6 million, supported by continued low credit losses and a loan portfolio described as low risk.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Income tax expense rose to €5.8 million from €4.5 million, and the effective tax rate increased from 12% to 17%.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Return on equity declined from 16.2% to 12.9%, while return on assets fell from 1.6% to 1.2%.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The net loan portfolio grew 19%, or €340 million, to €2.11 billion, exceeding €2 billion for the first time.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Business loans increased 27% to €986 million, and home and other private loans grew 17% to €863 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Customer deposits rose 9% to €2.05 billion, with demand deposits up 11% and term deposits up 8%.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: The customer base increased by 19,000, or 9%, to 227,000.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: The operating environment improved as Estonia’s economy returned to modest growth, inflation receded and interest rates declined.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Estonian home and business lending grew approximately 10% market-wide, supporting demand for Coop Pank’s financing products, but falling rates constrained the bank’s interest income.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: The bank strengthened funding by issuing €250 million of four-year covered bonds, its first international covered-bond issuance, and began reducing more expensive term and foreign deposits.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: It also entered into an EIB Group guarantee arrangement expected to enable up to €249 million of new business lending, while a €5 million EEEF subordinated loan was drawn in February 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Moody’s affirmed the bank’s Baa2 deposit rating with a positive outlook.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Regulatory capital requirements were met, although the CET1 ratio declined slightly to 14.15% from 14.28% and total capital adequacy to 18.54% from 19.41%.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: The bank paid €7.2 million in dividends for 2024, or €0.07 per share, and proposed a 2025 dividend of €0.065 per share.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1 (profitability metrics), K2 (loan portfolio growth), K3 (deposit growth), K4 (customer base expansion), K6 (funding and guarantees), K7 (capital ratios), K10 (dividends), and K11 (EEEF loan). However, it omits the strategic targets outlined in K5, sustainability initiatives described in K8, product/service launches mentioned in K9, and the management board appointment in K12. These omissions are material for K5 (HIGH importance) and represent significant missing components for the MEDIUM items (K8, K9, K12). The summary captures most HIGH-importance items but lacks one HIGH item (K5) and several MEDIUM items, resulting in a Generally yes rating.
